examples.ko: 할머니가 사발에 밥을 가득 담아 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother filled a bowl to the brim with rice.
The soup in the bowl is still hot.
The country house has many old bowls.

examples.ko: 설날에 떡국을 큰 사발에 담아 먹었어요.
examples.en: On Lunar New Year's Day we ate rice cake soup from a big bowl.
I poured water into a bowl and gave it to the dog.
The bowl is big, so hold it with two hands.

explain: 밥이나 국을 담는 크고 우묵한 그릇이에요. 보통 쓰는 '밥그릇'보다 크고 옛날식 느낌이 있어서 시골집이나 전통 음식 이야기에서 잘 나와요. '사발면'이라는 라면 이름에도 이 말이 들어 있어요.

phrases.example: 배가 고파서 밥 한 사발을 다 먹었어요.
phrases.en: I was hungry, so I ate a whole bowl of rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양이 푸짐하다는 느낌이 있어서 '한 사발'로 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It feels generous in amount, so it is often said as 한 사발.

phrases.en: I ate cup noodles at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사발 모양 그릇에 담긴 라면을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Instant noodles that come in a bowl-shaped container.

phrases.en: I filled a big bowl with soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사발은 원래 크니까 '큰'을 붙여 더 크다는 것을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sabal is already large, so adding 큰 stresses the size.

explain_en: It is a large, deep dish for rice or soup. It is bigger than an ordinary '밥그릇' and feels old-fashioned, so it often appears in stories about country homes and traditional food. The word is also part of the noodle product name '사발면'.

examples.en: I put the greens in a basket.
I scooped the boiled noodles out with a basket strainer.
I bought a bamboo basket at the market.
Grandma gave me a basketful of potatoes.
A basket like this has holes, so the water drains out.
I need one more basket.

explain: 대나무나 싸리로 엮어 둥글고 넓게 만든 그릇으로, 물기를 빼거나 채소를 담을 때 써요. 뭐든 담는 '바구니'보다 부엌이나 시장 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.example: 씻은 채소를 소쿠리에 올려 물기를 빼요.
phrases.en: I put the washed vegetables in a basket to drain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소쿠리의 쓰임을 가장 잘 보여 주는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This pairing shows the most typical use of a 소쿠리.

phrases.en: I dug up a basketful of potatoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그릇이 가득 찬 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a basket filled to the brim.

phrases.en: I put the groceries in a basket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 넓은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요. 소쿠리는 엮어서 만든 것을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word for basket; 소쿠리 is specifically a woven one.

explain_en: Open woven basket for draining or storing washed vegetables or rice. It is a wide, round container woven from bamboo or similar material, used to drain water or hold vegetables. Compared with the all-purpose '바구니', it has a stronger kitchen or market feel.

en: to be small and neat; to be cozy

examples.en: This cafe is small but cozy.
The room is small and neat, so it's easy to clean.
The house is decorated in a small, tidy way.
A small, neat hanok stands at the end of the alley.

examples.ko: 아담할 줄 알았는데 안은 생각보다 넓었어요.
examples.en: I thought it would be small, but inside it was bigger than I expected.
I chose a small, pretty gift box.

explain: 작지만 단정하고 보기 좋은 집, 방, 가게, 체형에 써요. 그냥 '작다'와 달리 칭찬하는 느낌이 있어서 좁고 불편한 곳에는 쓰지 않아요. 크기가 작다는 느낌이 꼭 들어가서 '예쁘다'만 뜻하지는 않아요.

phrases.example: 언덕 위에 아담한 집이 한 채 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a small, neat house on the hill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸미는 활용형으로, 작지만 보기 좋은 곳을 칭찬해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, praising a place that is small but pleasant.

phrases.en: This room is small but looks neat and cozy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습에서 받은 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an impression based on appearance.

phrases.en: I decorated the small shop in a neat, cozy way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 공간을 예쁘고 단정하게 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when making a small space look tidy and pleasant.

explain_en: Small but tidy and pleasant; rooms, cafes, houses (아담한 카페) Use it for a house, room, shop, or build that is small but tidy and pleasant. Unlike plain 작다 it is a compliment, so it is not used for places that are cramped and uncomfortable. It always carries a sense of small size, so it does not simply mean pretty.

t90.ax: This cafe is small but cozy.

examples.ko: 자판을 빨리 치는 연습을 하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm practicing typing fast.
I spilled coffee on the laptop keyboard.

examples.ko: 이 자판은 누를 때 소리가 작아요.
examples.en: This keyboard is quiet when you press it.

examples.ko: 자판 위치를 외우면 글을 빨리 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you memorize the key positions, you can write fast.

examples.ko: 한글 자판과 영어 자판을 바꿔 가며 써요.
examples.en: I switch between the Korean and English keyboard layouts.
The keyboard is worn and the letters have faded.

explain: 컴퓨터나 타자기에서 글자를 치는 판이에요. 일상에서는 '키보드'를 더 많이 쓰고, '자판'은 글자 배열(한글 자판, 쿼티 자판)을 말할 때 자주 써요. 숫자나 계산기 버튼판은 '키패드'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I bought a new keyboard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자판'과 뜻이 같고, 일상에서는 '키보드'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 자판; 키보드 is more common in daily life.

phrases.example: 밤에는 자판을 치는 소리가 크게 들려요.
phrases.en: The sound of typing is loud at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자를 입력할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for typing.

phrases.en: I've gotten used to the Hangeul keyboard layout.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자 배열을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about the key layout.

explain_en: The keys you type on; native Sino-Korean word, more formal. It is the board of keys for typing on a computer or typewriter. In daily talk 키보드 is more common; 자판 often refers to the key layout, such as 한글 자판 or 쿼티 자판. For a number or calculator pad, people say 키패드.

examples.en: We keep potatoes in the underground storage room.
The temperature in this storehouse is always constant.
The food store is almost empty.

examples.ko: 농부들이 마을 저장고에 쌀을 쌓아 뒀어요.
examples.en: The farmers piled rice in the village storehouse.

examples.ko: 저장고 문을 열자 서늘한 공기가 나왔어요.
examples.en: When I opened the storeroom door, cool air came out.
We saved money to build a new storehouse.

explain: '창고'는 물건을 넣어 두는 건물 전체에 쓰고, '저장고'는 식량·물·에너지처럼 오래 모아 두는 것에 어울려요. 컴퓨터 자료를 두는 곳은 '저장소'나 '저장 공간'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 겨울을 위해 식량 저장고를 가득 채웠어요.
phrases.en: We filled the food storehouse for winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹을 것을 오래 모아 두는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a place where food is stored for a long time.

phrases.en: I keep kimchi in the underground storage room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅 밑에 만든 저장고를 말할 때 앞에 '지하'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 지하 before 저장고 for a storage room built underground.

phrases.en: I put my things in the warehouse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 창고는 물건을 넣어 두는 건물에 널리 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 창고 is a broad word for a building where things are kept.

explain_en: '창고' covers any building for keeping goods, while '저장고' fits things stored for a long time, such as food, water or energy. For computer data, people say '저장소' or '저장 공간'.

examples.en: I glued the broken cup back together.
The glue got on my hand and won't come off.
This adhesive sticks well to wood.
Don't apply too much glue.
You have to wait until the glue dries.
I bought a strong adhesive at the store.

explain: 일상에서는 '풀'과 '본드'를 더 많이 말해요. '풀'은 종이에, '본드'는 나무나 플라스틱 같은 단단한 것에 쓰는 접착제예요. 가게에서 '접착제'라고 해도 다 알아들어요.

phrases.en: I stick paper together with glue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 종이를 붙일 때 '접착제'보다 '풀'을 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, people say 풀 more than 접착제 for sticking paper.

phrases.en: I fixed the wooden chair with strong glue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무나 플라스틱처럼 단단한 것을 붙일 때 '본드'를 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 본드 is common for hard things like wood or plastic.

phrases.en: Please spread the glue thinly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바르다'와 함께 접착제를 쓰는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with 바르다 to describe applying glue.

explain_en: In daily life people say '풀' and '본드' more often. '풀' is for paper and '본드' is for hard things like wood or plastic. Saying '접착제' at a store is understood by everyone.

examples.en: I tidied the room cleanly on the weekend.
Before an interview I neaten my hair.

examples.ko: 책장을 정돈하는 데 한 시간쯤 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took about an hour to tidy up the bookshelf.
I'll talk after I put my thoughts in order.
If you arrange clothes by color, they are easy to find.
I need time to put the documents in order.

explain: 정돈하다는 흩어진 물건이나 생각을 가지런히 놓는다는 말이에요. '청소하다'는 먼지와 쓰레기를 치우는 일이고, 정돈하다는 제자리에 놓는 일이에요. 일상에서는 '정리하다'를 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I tidied up the top of my desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '정돈하다' 대신 '정리하다'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday conversation, 정리하다 is used much more than 정돈하다.

phrases.en: I take a moment to sort out my thoughts before presenting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 복잡한 생각을 차분하게 가다듬을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when calmly sorting out complicated thoughts.

phrases.en: I'll put the books on the shelf and keep them tidy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 두다'를 붙여 정돈한 상태를 계속 유지한다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 두다 gives the sense of keeping things in a tidy state.
phrases.en_equiv: to set in order and leave

explain_en: Active: someone tidies something up (책장을 정돈하다) 정돈하다 means to arrange scattered things or thoughts neatly. 청소하다 is cleaning away dust and trash, while 정돈하다 is putting things in their place. In daily talk 정리하다 is more common.

examples.ko: 실험할 때는 수돗물 대신 증류수를 써요.
examples.en: In experiments we use distilled water instead of tap water.
Distilled water tastes flat, so it's not great to drink.
We ran out of distilled water, so I couldn't turn on the humidifier.

examples.ko: 약을 증류수에 녹인 다음 주사기로 뽑았어요.
examples.en: I dissolved the medicine in distilled water and drew it up with a syringe.
I bought a bottle of distilled water at the supermarket.

examples.ko: 가습기에는 증류수로 물을 채우는 게 좋대요.
examples.en: I heard it's better to fill the humidifier with distilled water.

explain: 과학 시간 실험에서 자주 들어요. 생수나 정수와 달리 마시는 물보다 실험, 가습기, 다리미에 쓰는 물로 생각하면 쉬워요.

phrases.en: I wiped the glass with distilled water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨끗한 물이 필요한 청소나 실험에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for cleaning or experiments needing very clean water.

phrases.en: I put distilled water in the humidifier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가습기나 다리미처럼 기계에 물을 넣을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when adding water to a machine like a humidifier or iron.

phrases.en: I brought a bottle of distilled water from the lab.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물의 양을 세는 '병'과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with the counter 병 to count bottles of water.

explain_en: You often hear it in science-class experiments. Unlike bottled or purified water, think of it as water for experiments, humidifiers and irons rather than for drinking.

examples.en: They made fried rice for us on the griddle.
The griddle is hot, so be careful.
They laid thick iron plates on the floor of the construction site.
Squid grilled on a griddle is really good.
It's a door made of iron plate, so it's hard to open.

examples.ko: 철판은 열이 오래 가서 고기를 굽기 좋아요.
examples.en: An iron griddle holds heat for long, so it is good for grilling meat.

explain: 요리에서는 '철판 볶음밥'처럼 두꺼운 판에 굽는 음식을 말할 때 써요. 공사장이나 공장에서는 두꺼운 쇠판을 가리켜요. 사람에게 쓰면 '철판을 깔다'처럼 아주 뻔뻔하다는 뜻이 돼요.

phrases.example: 그는 얼굴에 철판을 깔고 다시 부탁했어요.
phrases.en: to have a lot of nerve; to be shameless
phrases.nuance_ko: 창피한 줄 모르는 뻔뻔한 모습을 말해요. 보통 좋지 않게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes someone who has no sense of shame. It is usually said in a negative way.

explain_en: In cooking it is used for food grilled on a thick plate, as in '철판 볶음밥'. At construction sites and factories it means a thick sheet of iron. In an expression about people, '철판을 깔다', it means being very shameless.

en: to be dense; to be thick; to be closely woven

examples.en: This sweater is tightly knit, so it is warm.
Even small fish got caught in the fine net.
I saw a night sky studded with densely packed stars.
My schedule this week is too packed.
If you write the letters too close together, it is hard to read.

examples.ko: 빗살이 촘촘하고 가늘어서 머리가 잘 빗어져요.
examples.en: The comb's teeth are close together and thin, so it combs hair well.

explain: 간격이 좁고 빽빽할 때 써요. 반대는 '성기다'나 '듬성듬성'이에요. 물건뿐 아니라 '일정이 촘촘하다'처럼 시간이 꽉 찬 상황에도 써요. '빽빽하다'는 사람이나 나무가 많이 모여 있을 때 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The stitching is tight, so the clothes are sturdy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 앞에서 간격을 좁게 한다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a verb, it adds the meaning of leaving small gaps.

phrases.example: 이번 주는 일정이 촘촘해서 쉴 시간이 없어요.
phrases.en: My schedule is packed this week, so I have no time to rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간이 꽉 차 있을 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can also be used when time is fully booked.

phrases.example: 이 천은 짜임이 촘촘하지 않아서 바람이 잘 통해요.
phrases.en: This fabric isn't tightly woven, so air passes through well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 간격이 넓다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative it shows that the gaps are wide.

explain_en: Closely spaced — fine gaps, like stitches, weave or mesh (이 스웨터는 실이 촘촘해서 겨울에 아주 따뜻해요.) It describes narrow, tight gaps. The opposite is '성기다' or '듬성듬성'. Besides objects, it fits a full schedule, as in '일정이 촘촘하다'. '빽빽하다' sounds more natural when many people or trees are crowded together.

t90.ax: My schedule this week is too packed.

examples.en: I board near the university.

examples.ko: 처음 서울에 왔을 때 학교 앞에서 하숙했어요.
examples.en: When I first came to Seoul, I lodged near the school.

examples.ko: 하숙하면 밥을 해 먹지 않아도 돼서 편해요.
examples.en: If you board, you don't have to cook, so it's convenient.
Where do you want to board?
While I boarded, the landlady was good to me.
I plan to board for a short while only during vacation.

explain: 방을 빌리면서 식사도 함께 받는 것을 말해요. 식사 없이 혼자 밥을 해 먹으며 사는 '자취하다'와 달라요. 사는 집은 '하숙집', 사람은 '하숙생'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I'm boarding near my school now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하숙 생활을 하는 중이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you are currently living in a boarding house.

phrases.example: 하숙집 아주머니가 밥을 맛있게 해 주세요.
phrases.en: The landlady of my boarding house cooks tasty meals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하숙하는 집이나 그 건물을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The house or building where one boards.

phrases.en: I am a boarder in this house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하숙하는 사람을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who boards.

explain_en: To rent a room with meals at someone's home. It means renting a room and getting meals along with it. This differs from '자취하다', where you live alone and cook for yourself. The house is a '하숙집' and the person is a '하숙생'.

t90.ax: Where do you want to board?

en: to go through hardships; to have difficulty

examples.ko: 우리 부모님은 젊을 때 고생고생하며 사셨어요.
examples.en: My parents lived through many hardships when they were young.
I had a really hard time all week because of moving.

examples.ko: 그 길을 찾느라 고생고생해서 겨우 도착했어요.
examples.en: I struggled so much to find the way that I barely arrived.
I am thankful to my mother, who went through so much raising children.
I have so much luggage that I am struggling on the stairs.
After going through so much hardship, I finally passed.

explain: '고생하다'를 반복해서 힘든 일을 오래, 많이 겪었다는 느낌을 더해요. 하소연하거나 지난 일을 이야기할 때 잘 어울려요. 윗사람에게는 '고생고생하시다'처럼 높여요.

phrases.en: After going through so much hardship, I finally bought a house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들게 노력한 끝에 결과를 얻었다는 말을 이어 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links the hardship to the result achieved afterward.

phrases.en: Grandmother went through so much hardship raising us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람의 힘든 일을 높여서 말하는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form for an older person's hardships.

phrases.en: I had a really hard time moving.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고생고생하다'보다 덜 하소연하는 느낌이라 일상에서 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less of a complaint than 고생고생하다; easy to use in daily talk.

explain_en: It repeats '고생하다' to add the feeling of having gone through hard things for a long time. It fits venting or telling stories about the past. For elders, make it honorific like '고생고생하시다'.

en: to nod; to bob slightly; to bob head

examples.en: The child bobs his head to the song.

examples.ko: 그녀는 알겠다는 듯 고개를 까닥거리며 웃었어요.
examples.en: She smiled, nodding slightly as if she understood.
Why do you keep bobbing your toes?
Grandfather just nodded slightly without a word.
He beckoned me by flicking his finger.

examples.ko: 친구는 제 이야기에 고개를 까닥거리면서 들었어요.
examples.en: My friend listened to my story, nodding slightly now and then.

explain: 한 번이 아니라 가볍게 여러 번 반복하는 느낌이에요. 한 번만 숙이는 동작은 '까닥'이라고 부사로 말해요. 리듬을 탈 때나 대답 대신 고개를 움직일 때 모두 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The child was sleepy and bobbed his head.
phrases.nuance_ko: '까닥거리다'와 비슷하지만 한두 번 움직일 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 까닥거리다 but more natural for one or two movements.

phrases.en: I bob my head along to the music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 동작이 반복된다는 느낌을 부사로 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb conveys the same small motion repeated.

phrases.en: He listened to my story with little nods.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'를 붙이면 다른 동작과 동시에 일어난다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -며 shows the nodding happens during another action.

explain_en: Head bobs lightly again and again, e.g. to music. It gives the feeling of repeating a light movement several times. A single dip is expressed with the adverb '까닥'. You can use it for moving to a rhythm or for nodding in place of an answer.

t90.ax: Why do you keep bobbing your toes?

en: to jump; to leap; to hop

examples.en: The puppy is so happy that it bounces around.
The kids play in the snow, leaping about.
A rabbit hopped across the meadow.
I was so excited that I bounded around and fell.

examples.ko: 왜 그렇게 껑충거려요? 무슨 좋은 일 있어요?
examples.en: Why are you bouncing like that? Did something good happen?

examples.ko: 그 사람은 다리가 길어서 껑충거리며 걸어요.
examples.en: He has long legs and walks with long bouncing strides.

explain: '껑충 뛰다'가 한 번 뛰는 것이라면, '껑충거리다'는 긴 다리로 계속 뛰어오르거나 큰 걸음으로 걷는 모습이에요. 작고 가벼운 동물에는 '깡충거리다'를 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: The child is so happy that he hops around.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 뛰어다니는 모습을 부사 '껑충껑충'으로 더 생생하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb 껑충껑충 makes the repeated leaping more vivid.

phrases.en: The deer leapt and crossed the stream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번 크게 뛰어오르는 것이라 '껑충거리다'와 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a single big jump, unlike the repeated 껑충거리다.

phrases.en: The calf is bounding around in the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: '껑충거리다'와 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 껑충거리다.

explain_en: Bigger, longer-legged leaps, like an excited dog. '껑충 뛰다' is a single leap, while '껑충거리다' means leaping repeatedly or walking with long bouncing strides. For small, light animals, '깡충거리다' is also used.

t90.ax: A rabbit hopped across the meadow.

en: to hammer away; to bang around noisily

examples.en: My father hammered away in the yard and made a chair.

examples.ko: 옆집에서 아침부터 뚝딱거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The neighbors were banging away from morning, so I couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 하루 종일 뚝딱거리는 소리가 나요.
examples.en: There's a banging sound from the construction site all day.

examples.ko: 남편이 주말마다 뚝딱거리면 선반이 하나씩 생겨요.
examples.en: Every weekend my husband tinkers away and a new shelf appears.
My grandfather has been hammering and tinkering all day.

examples.ko: 작은 책꽂이는 한 시간쯤 뚝딱거렸더니 완성됐어요.
examples.en: After about an hour of hammering away, the small bookshelf was done.

explain: 망치질하거나 뭔가를 만들 때 나는 두드리는 소리와 그렇게 만드는 모습이에요. '뚝딱'만 쓰면 '뚝딱 만들다'처럼 금방 해치운다는 느낌이 되지만, '-거리다'는 소리가 이어지는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: I've been hearing hammering sounds since morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두드리는 소리가 이어질 때 '-는 소리'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as '-는 소리' when the hammering keeps going.

phrases.en: My younger brother hammered away and made a bookshelf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두드리면서 무언가를 만드는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes making something while hammering.

phrases.en: They hammer all day long at the construction site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속되는 일을 해요체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite present form for something ongoing.

explain_en: It describes the pounding sounds of hammering or building something and the act of tinkering. '뚝딱' alone, as in '뚝딱 만들다', gives a sense of doing it quickly, while '-거리다' emphasizes the continuing sound.
